title: One-step compatibility of local Frobenius return transport
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], coefficient datum c and finite coefficient field E [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a finite-type k_0-scheme Y_0 [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and a Weil complex K [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Put Y=Y_0×_(k_0)k, g=g_Y and h=g_s [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let x,x':Spec(k)→Y satisfy xg=hx'. For r=n+1>0 assume xg^r=h^r x and x'g^r=h^r x'. Use exactly the rational pullback comparisons and point transports of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Define A:C_(x')→C_x by point transport on Lx'^*K, the inverse comparison for hx', the equality hx'=xg, the comparison for xg, and pullback of the Weil structure theta. Then A is invertible and A≫F_x=F_(x')≫A, where F_x and F_(x') are the prescribed length-r return operators. This compares only consecutive semilinear points; it asserts neither transitivity of residue embeddings nor conjugacy on cohomology.

proof.text: Put s=Spec(k), h=g_s, g=g_Y, M=For(K), and r=n+1. For any point z:s→Y let J_z(N)=Fib_s(Lz^*N). Given xg=hx' define tau:J_(x')(N)→J_x(GN) by iota_(Lx'^*N) followed by c_(h,x')^(-1), the equality hx'=xg, and c_(x,g). All compositions are the specified ones in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Point-transport naturality and naturality of the integral pullback comparison, after rational localization, make tau natural in N. Its value followed by J_x(theta) is precisely localFrobeniusStepTransport, not an arbitrary fibre isomorphism.

Define reparametrized successive points z_i=h^(-i)xg^i. The assumed one-step square gives z_0=x and z_1=x'. The return equation xg^r=h^r x gives z_(i+r)=z_i by commuting powers and cancellation. The same equations imply z_i g^m=z_(i+m)h^m. Define tau_i by the preceding construction. Equality of points identifies J_(i+r)=J_i and tau_(i+r)=tau_i, since all equality proofs are propositions. No false fixed-point equality xg^r=x is used.

Let Q_(i,m):J_(i+m)(N)→J_i(G^mN) be the composite of the m successive tau maps, with Q_(i,0)=id. Induct on m to identify it with the specified m-fold point transport followed by composition comparison. At zero both maps are identities; at one it is the definition. In the successor step use naturality of iota to move the identification Lz_(i+1)^*G^mN≅L(h^m)^*Lz_(i+m+1)^*N past the next iota. The remaining iota composite is exactly the defining recursion for I^[m+1]. Associativity of the integral comparison, rationalized using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], identifies the remaining comparison with c for g^(m+1)z_i=z_(i+m+1)h^(m+1).

Put A_i=J_i(theta)tau_i(M) and P_(i,m)=A_i...A_(i+m-1). Induct to prove P_(i,m)=J_i(theta^[m])Q_(i,m)(M). The zero case is identity. In the successor case move J_(i+1)(theta^[m]) through tau_i by naturality, then combine J_i(theta) and J_i(G theta^[m]) using functoriality. The equality theta^[m+1]=theta G(theta^[m]) follows by expanding the defining recursion and reassociating its m+1 Weil factors with the coherent pullback comparisons. Together with the preceding induction, this is the required successor identity. Taking m=r and using z_(i+r)=z_i identifies P_(i,r) with the actual localFrobeniusOperator at z_i.

By periodicity A_r=A_0, so the two words P_(0,r)A_0 and A_0 P_(1,r) are equal: each is A_0 A_1 ... A_(r-1) A_0. In Lean composition order this reads A_0≫F_x=F_(x')≫A_0, the asserted equation. This also proves the r=1 case, with one Weil factor, and the zero-complex case. Invertibility of the explicitly constructed A_0 is proved separately in Lean from point-transport invertibility, instantiated on the identity finite-type model Spec(k_0), and the isomorphism factors in its definition; it is not an extra hypothesis on this equation.

theorem localFrobeniusStepCompatibility (n : ℕ)
    (hx : x ≫ localPositivePower (D.geometricFrobenius Y₀).hom n =
      localPositivePower (frobeniusPointIso D).hom n ≫ x)
    (hx' : x' ≫ localPositivePower (D.geometricFrobenius Y₀).hom n =
      localPositivePower (frobeniusPointIso D).hom n ≫ x') :
    localFrobeniusStepTransport D c E Y₀ K x x' hs ≫
        localFrobeniusOperator c.l E.val D c.different Y₀ K x n hx =
      localFrobeniusOperator c.l E.val D c.different Y₀ K x' n hx' ≫
        localFrobeniusStepTransport D c E Y₀ K x x' hs
